query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a specific element, such as Fe, to a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy can improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance by stabilizing the solid solution, suppressing pest oxidation, and forming a stable Cr-rich phase.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of Fe to the alloy
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation at 700-900 °C, room temperature hardness and compression testing
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable Cr-rich phase and suppression of pest oxidation
generation.mechanism: Stabilization of the solid solution and formation of a stable Cr-rich phase, which improves the alloy's mechanical and corrosion properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy without Fe addition
generation.boundary: Alloy composition, temperature range, and testing conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Fe to be added and the optimal testing conditions are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation properties of the as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with and without Fe addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Fe does not improve the combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance of the alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: In this work, the RM(Nb)IC alloy Nb–30Ti–10Si–5Cr–5Sn–3Fe–2Al–2Hf (NV2) was studied in the as-cast and heat-treated conditions; its isothermal oxidation at 700, 800 and 900 °C and its room temperature hardness and specific strength were compared with other Sn-containing RM(Nb)ICs—in particular, the alloy Nb–24Ti–18Si–5Cr–5Fe–5Sn (NV5)—and with RCCAs and RHEAs. The addition of Fe (a) stabilised Nbss; A15–Nb3X (X = Al, Si and Sn) and Nb3Si; metastable Nb3Si-m’ and Nb5Si3 silicides; (b) supported the formation of eutectic Nbss + Nb5Si3; (c) suppressed pest oxidation at all three temperatures and (d) stabilised a Cr- and Fe-rich phase instead of a C14–Nb(Cr,Fe)2 Laves phase. Complex concentrated (or compositionally complex) and/or high entropy phases co-existed with “conventional” phases in all conditions and after oxidation at 800 °C. In NV2, the macrosegregation of Si decreased but liquation occurred at T >1200 °C. A solid solution free of Si and rich in Cr and Ti was stable after the heat treatments. In this work, alloy Nb–30Ti–10Si–5Cr–5Sn–3Fe–2Al–2Hf (NV2) was studied in the as-cast and heat-treated conditions: its isothermal oxidation at three pest oxidation temperatures and its room temperature hardness and specific strength were evaluated and compared with other Sn-containing RM(Nb)ICs—in particular, alloy NV5—and with RCCAs and RHEAs. The issues that motivated this research were resolved. The synergy of Fe with Al, Cr, Hf and Sn (a) stabilised Nbss; A15–Nb3X (X = Al, Si and Sn) and Nb3Si, metastable Nb3Si-m’ and Nb5Si3 silicides; (b) supported the formation of Nbss + Nb5Si3 eutectic in the cast microstructure; (c) suppressed pest oxidation in the temperature range 700–900 °C and (d) stabilised a Cr-rich π phase instead of a C14–Nb(Cr,Fe)2 Laves phase. Furthermore, it was shown that complex concentrated (CC) or high entropy (HE) phases coexisted with “conventional” phases in all conditions and after oxidation at 800 °C.
